characterization_methods.key_findings: Room temperature: yield stress 601 MPa (compression) and 427 MPa (tension), total elongation 1.4%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1; compression samples (6×6×10) mm³; tension flat samples (3.5×5) mm², 15 mm gauge length; elevated-temperature tests in protective argon, held 30 min at test temperature, NiCr–Ni thermocouple on specimen surface
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine yield stress in compression/tension, total elongation and work-hardening behaviour

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: load 62.5 g, indentation ball 2.5 mm diameter
SEM-Hitachi S-530, 20 kV, working distance 15 mm
characterization_methods.key_findings: Very fine facetted transgranular cleavage (TGC); Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C has the highest ductility (1.4%) of all Fe-26Al-based alloys.
characterization_methods.purpose: Investigate fracture surfaces of ruptured tensile specimens

interfaces.phase_evolution: Fe-26Al-based matrix undergoes D0₃→B2 order-disorder transition at ~550 °C and B2→A2 at ~800 °C before melting.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Room-temperature total elongation: Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C = 1.4% (highest of all Fe-26Al-based alloys), compared with binary Fe-26Al = 0.4%

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase: Fe3Al matrix with MC (NbC) carbides

unmapped_findings: Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C exhibits lower yield stress in compression (601 MPa) than binary Fe-26Al (644 MPa) but shows much stronger work hardening during plastic deformation (b0024, b0027).
Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C shows tension–compression asymmetry: yield stress in compression is higher than in tension at room temperature, 650 °C and 800 °C (b0029, b0040).
At elevated temperatures, the yield stress anomaly peak of Nb-containing Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C is shifted towards lower temperatures and higher stresses relative to binary Fe-26Al (b0038).
Room-temperature fracture mode: transgranular cleavage (TGC) with very fine facetted cleavage; Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C has the highest ductility (1.4%) of all Fe-26Al-based alloys (b0033, b0035).
Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C (Nb addition) shows higher matrix hardness than binary Fe-26Al (275 HB vs 260 HB) (b0021, b0033).
